title: Windows CC build fails with compiler/linker out-of-memory errors under high parallelism
signature: Windows Release build runs out of memory - compiler fatal error C1060 (out of heap space) and linker fatal error LNK1102 (out of memory) under high parallelism|Infrastructure

failed_jobs.name: Conditional Compilation
failed_jobs.symptom: MSBuild 'Cmake build - CC ON' step fails: MSVC cl.exe reports fatal error C1060 (compiler is out of heap space) across dozens of onednn/CPU-plugin/frontend translation units, followed by MSB4018 OutOfMemoryException from the CL task.

key_errors: C:\BuildTools\VC\Tools\MSVC\14.42.34433\include\type_traits(540,1): error C1060: compiler is out of heap space [...\dnnl_common.vcxproj]
c1xx : fatal  error C1060: compiler is out of heap space [...\dnnl_common.vcxproj]
C:\actions-runner\_work\openvino\openvino\openvino\src\plugins\intel_cpu\thirdparty\onednn\src\common\group_normalization.cpp(233,1): error C1060: compiler is out of heap space
C:\BuildTools\MSBuild\Microsoft\VC\v170\Microsoft.CppCommon.targets(755,5): error MSB4018: The "CL" task failed unexpectedly. [...\openvino_runtime_obj.vcxproj]

C:\BuildTools\MSBuild\Microsoft\VC\v170\Microsoft.CppCommon.targets(755,5): error MSB4018: System.AggregateException: One or more errors occurred. ---> System.OutOfMemoryException: Exception of type 'System.OutOfMemoryException' was thrown.
cl : command line  warning D9014: invalid value '15' for '/cgthreads'; assuming '4'
root_cause: The Windows Conditional Compilation build runs MSBuild with a high degree of parallelism (/cgthreads requested at 15, clamped to 4 per-TU, combined with many parallel MSBuild projects) on a 16-core/32GB runner. Compiling heavy C++ template-heavy translation units (oneDNN, CPU plugin, frontend common_translators) simultaneously exhausts the 32-bit cl.exe/MSBuild process heap, producing cascading C1060 'out of heap space' errors across many .vcxproj files almost simultaneously, followed by an OutOfMemoryException inside the CL MSBuild task. This is a known, recurring infrastructure capacity issue (already recorded 22 times since 2026-11-03), not caused by the merged PR's code changes (a GPU oneDNN convolution preferred-format fix, unrelated to the Windows CC toolchain or build parallelism).
reproduction_steps: N/A - requires reproducing memory pressure on a 16-core/32GB Windows CC runner with the exact MSBuild parallelism/cgthreads configuration used by windows_conditional_compilation.yml; not reliably reproducible locally.
recommended_actions: Reduce MSBuild/cl.exe parallelism (MSBUILDDISABLENODEREUSE, /m:<n>, or /cgthreads) for the Windows CC job to lower peak per-process heap usage, trading build time for reliability.
Move the Windows Conditional Compilation job to a runner with more memory (e.g., 64GB) given this is the 22nd occurrence of the same signature in under three weeks.

Consider splitting the heaviest translation units (oneDNN common/cpu sources, openvino_common_translators) into smaller compilation batches or enabling /Zm (increase compiler memory limit) as a stopgap.
Escalate to the CI infrastructure owners given the persistent recurrence (count=22) - this should be treated as a standing infra ticket rather than a one-off investigation.
prevention_strategies: Track peak build memory usage in the Windows CC workflow and alert before C1060 occurs; cap MSBuild parallelism proportional to available RAM (recommend <= 1GB per concurrent cl.exe process for oneDNN/CPU-plugin heavy TUs); consider a dedicated higher-memory runner pool for Windows C++ builds.
historical_context: This exact signature (compiler/linker out-of-memory errors under high parallelism on the Windows CC build) has recurred 22 times since first recorded on 2026-11-03T07:07:04Z, most recently on 2026-11-23T17:11:33Z just one day prior to this run - confirming this is an ongoing, unresolved infrastructure capacity problem rather than a new code regression.
